earlier_scan.note: Tangshewi: ISO code tnf retired 2010, merged into Dari [prs]; Glottolog lists no descriptive source at all

sources.citation: Beck, Simone & Daniela Beyer. 2013. A Sociolinguistic Assessment of the Darwāzi Speech Variety in Afghanistan. Linguistic Discovery 11(1): 22-82. DOI 10.1349/PS1.1537-0852.A.396 (open access).
sources.note: No statement on stress anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent/suprasegmental/phonology yields only the Lorimer 1922 title). Sociolinguistic survey (Aug-Sep 2008) of 16 Darwaz villages incl. 3 Tangshew-valley villages; §2.3 p. 29: 'The Darwāzi people themselves refer to their language as Dari, Farsi or Tajik. They rarely use Darwāzi or Tangshewi for their speech variety. These names are given by linguists from the outside.'; §2.4 p. 29: 'Documented research into the Darwāzi and Tangshewi speech varieties is extremely rare.' Appendix A (pp. 67-72) is a 148-item IPA word list per village…

sources.citation: Goedemans, Rob. 2010. Word accent systems in the languages of Asia. In Harry van der Hulst, Rob Goedemans & Ellen van Zanten (eds.), A Survey of Word Accentual Patterns in the Languages of the World, 509-599. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Tangshewi appears only in the Ethnologue-derived Iranian family tree ('UNCLASSIFIED: Tangshewi', p. 564: 'R. Gordon (2005).. treats Tangshewi as unclassifiable'); no StressTyp entry for it. For 'Dari (dialect of Persian) [U]' (p. 565): 'Primary stress falls on the final syllable. Secondary stress is located on the initial syllable' (˙zendæ¨gi 'life', ˙ašpæzxa¨næ 'kitchen'); Western Farsi and Tajik: 'Stress falls on the final syllable.' Second-hand (StressTyp).

sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'This entry has been retired and is featured here only for bookkeeping purposes.. Retired in ISO 639-3: merge with [prs] Dari. Change request: 2009-027.. Effective: 2010-01-18.' The single Glottolog ref attached to this key (Longacre & Woods 1976, Colombia/Panama/Ecuador) is a misattribution and irrelevant.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 RA code page for tnf (Deprecated, retirement date 2010-01-18, reason Merge, into prs Dari).
sources.note: Nothing on stress; confirms retirement/merge only.

sources.citation: Beck, Simone (IAM). 2009. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2009-027: retire [tnf] Tangshewi, merge into [prs] Eastern Farsi (Dari). ISO 639-3 Registration Authority, adopted 2010-01-18.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Rationale (p. 2): 'Lexical similiarity of Dari and Tangshewi is between 86% and 90%. Comprehension testing of Eastern Farsi (Dari) showed that Dari is highly intelligible for the Tangshewi people.. No one ever mentioned a language called Tangshewi as his mother tongue. The Tangshewi themselves explain that they speak Dari, acknowledging that their dialect is slightly different.' Basis: first-hand survey visit (word lists, interviews, comprehension testing).

sources.citation: Gordon, Raymond G., Jr. (ed.). 2005. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 15th ed. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'Tangshewi' (web version, Internet Archive copy 2009-01-30).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Full entry: 'Population 10,000 (1994). Region East of Darwazi on the Amu Darya, far northeast of Badakhshan. May also be in Turkmenistan. Alternate names Tangshuri. Dialects May be Eastern Iranian. Probably closely related to Darwazi. Classification Indo-European, Indo-Iranian, Iranian, Unclassified.. May be called Tajiki. Muslim.' This entry is the sole origin of the 'language'.

sources.citation: Lorimer, D. L. R. 1922. The Phonology of the Bakhtiari, Badakhshani, and Madaglashti Dialects of Modern Persian, with Vocabularies. London: Royal Asiatic Society (Prize Publication Fund 6). archive.org item phonologyofbakht00loriuoft (public domain).
sources.note: Badakhshani Persian (the Darwaz-area variety per Beck & Beyer 2013 §2.4, but not Tangshew specifically). Part II preliminary notes (scanned ~p. 130): 'The stress accent, in a few cases where it has been specially noted, is marked by a vertical line over the vowel on which it falls, e.g. qalwa.' No rule for stress placement is given for Badakhshani; the Phonology section (p. 131 ff.) treats segments only.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia 'Tangshewi' and 'Darwazi language' (both redirect to Dari / Persian language); Russian Wikipedia 'Дарвазский диалект'.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; ru.wikipedia describes the Darvaz (Tajik-side) dialect as a south-eastern Tajik dialect group archaic in verb morphology (bə-/me- prefixes, postposed -me) and cites Kerimova 1997 (Tadžikskij jazyk, Jazyki mira: Iranskie jazyki I) and Lashkarbekov 2008 — not verified further.

sources.citation: Kerimova, A. A. 1997. Tadžikskij jazyk. In Jazyki mira: Iranskie jazyki I. Jugo-zapadnye iranskie jazyki. Moscow: Indrik. (cited by ru.wikipedia 'Дарвазский диалект' as the source for the Darvaz/south-eastern Tajik dialect group)

sources.note: The Darvaz dialects on the Tajik bank of the Panj are the closest documented relatives of the Darwazi/Tangshewi speech (Beck & Beyer 2013 report villagers saying Vanj/Tajik-side speech is 'exactly the same'); a Russian-academy sketch of Tajik dialects would state the stress rule (udarenie) for that dialect group. Bibliographic record seen only via ru.
